arguments.summary: Captured the quotation process. The sales employee receives a quotation request from a customer, records it in the quoting system, checks the customer's information in the CRM, and creates the quotation in the quoting system using customer and pricing data. If the quotation is over 1,000,000 yen, it must be approved by a manager (for credit risk management) before being sent to the customer; otherwise it goes directly to the customer. At month-end, the sales employee sends a summary of the quotation information to the Accounting team (rationale unknown). The manager's ability to reject or change the quotation is unknown.

observations.text: The process starts when we receive a quotation request from a customer. That's what triggers it, and we're the ones who receive it.
I'm the sales employee who handles the quotation requests from customers. I receive them, record them, and then work through the process.
After I receive the request, I record it, then I check the customer's information in the CRM.
I record the request into our quoting system.
After checking the customer's information in the CRM, I create the quotation using the customer and pricing information.
The pricing information comes from our pricing data, and yes, I create the quotation in the quoting system.
Yes, the pricing data is what I use when creating the quotation. It's the same thing as the pricing information.
After I create the quotation, if it's over 1,000,000 yen, it needs to be approved by a manager before it's sent. Otherwise, if it's at or below that amount, it goes directly to the customer.

I don't know if the manager can reject or change the quotation—that's not something I have information on. Once the quotation is sent to the customer, that's the end of the process for me, except at month-end I also send a summary of the quotation information to the Accounting team.
The approval is for credit risk management.
I don't know the reason for the month-end summary to Accounting. I only have a vague impression that Accounting needs it, but I'm not certain and there's no documentation.
I check the customer's information in the CRM to make sure we have the correct details before creating the quotation. It's just part of the normal process.
I record the request into the quoting system so we have a formal record of it before we proceed with the quotation.
I create the quotation so we can provide the customer with a formal price quote based on their request and our pricing data.
I send the quotation to the customer so they have the official price quote we've prepared for them.
Receiving the quotation request is the starting point of the whole process—it's what triggers us to begin preparing a quotation for the customer.
